content.text:
Lint didn't run (approval declined), but the change is one line and the test additions follow the file's existing style.

## Change

`lib/decorate.js:121` — `checkDependencies` now falls back to `hasInstanceProperty`:

```js
if (!checkExistence(instance, deps[i]) && !hasInstanceProperty(instance, deps[i])) {
  throw new FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY(deps[i])
}
```

This is the fourth call site that #6753 missed. `hasInstanceProperty` walks the `parent` chain checking `instanceProperties` (`Request`: `id, params, raw, query, log, body` — `lib/request.js:41`; `Reply`: `raw, request, log` — `lib/reply.js:80`), so constructor-assigned built-ins now resolve the same way they already do for `hasRequestDecorator`/`hasReplyDecorator` and the `FST_ERR_DEC_ALREADY_PRESENT` guard.

The instance path (`decorate()` → plain Fastify instance) is unaffected: no `instanceProperties`/`parent` on it, so the loop exits immediately and returns `false`. Ordinary decorator deps still short-circuit on `checkExistence`.

## Tests

Appended five cases to `test/decorator-instance-properties.test.js`: full built-in sets accepted as deps for both `Request` and `Reply`, an encapsulated plugin exercising the `parent` chain, a mixed built-in/user-decorator dep array, and a regression case asserting unknown deps still throw `FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` plus a `Reply` decorator depending on the `Request`-only `body` still throwing.

`node --test test/decorator-instance-properties.test.js` → 11/11 pass. Per your instruction I ran only that one file, and I did not commit.

One caveat on the issue's claim that the new tests fail on the base commit: I didn't empirically verify that (it would have required reverting the file mid-session). By inspection it holds — pre-fix, `checkExistence(Request, 'body')` checks `'body' in Request`, `'body' in Request.prototype` and `props`, none of which see a constructor-assigned property, so the positive cases would throw `FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY`.
